newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy Ross says Hebron deal not concluded.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross says Hebron deal not concluded.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said on Monday work remained to conclude a deal on an Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"There is work going on. There is still a lot of work to be done," Ross told reporters upon entering talks under way between Palestinian and Israeli officials on Hebron.
"I think there are still issues to be resolved I think you should focus on the facts that there is more work to be done," Ross said when asked if an agreement on Hebron was close.
Ross, who shuttled between Israel, PLO-ruled Gaza and Egypt since his arrival on Saturday, held talks on Monday evening with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other senior Israeli officials.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, asked after the meeting if Ross was about to leave Israel, said: "No, no." Levy did not say how long Ross would remain in the region.
Earlier Palestinian and Israeli negotiators said progress had been made in the U.S.-brokered talks to break a deadlock over Hebron by Christmas.
